extra.message: The body of the response from fetch('http://localhost:9000/inject/eval') (line 35) is passed directly to eval(), executing it as JavaScript in the page context. The fetch uses cleartext HTTP and the content is never validated, so a man-in-the-middle or compromised remote server can execute arbitrary code in the application (eval injection).

The base class resultDisplay renders this.props.genericInput via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. genericInput originates from the user-editable textarea in the root App component (App.js line 66), and this resultDisplay is inherited by multiple components (e.g. Vulnerable, Safe), so user-controlled values are injected as raw HTML, bypassing React's escaping and enabling arbitrary script execution via event handlers (XSS).

InnerElement renders props.genericInput via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. genericInput is passed down from the root App component's user-editable textarea, so user-controlled values are injected as raw HTML, allowing arbitrary event-handler script execution (XSS).

The anchor href is set from this.state.href, which is copied directly from the user-controlled form input on submit (line 13) without validation or URL scheme whitelisting. A value such as 'javascript:alert(1)' creates a link that executes script when clicked (XSS); arbitrary URLs also enable open redirects.

this.props.genericInput, which originates from the root App component's user-editable textarea, is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, allowing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript injection and event-handler execution (XSS).

In componentDidMount (lines 20-26), each window.location.search query parameter is decoded and concatenated into an HTML string that is stored in state and rendered here via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. An attacker-controlled query parameter such as '<div onmouseover=alert(1)>' executes script in the victim's browser (DOM-based XSS from the URL).

this.props.genericInput, which originates from the root App component's user-editable textarea, is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, allowing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript injection and event-handler execution (XSS).

this.state.submittedFormValue, copied directly from the user-controlled form input on submit (line 6), is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. This bypasses React's default escaping and allows injection of arbitrary HTML and event handlers such as <div onmouseover=alert(1)> (XSS).

this.props.genericInput, which originates from the root App component's user-editable textarea, is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, allowing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript injection and event-handler execution (XSS).

On submit, this.state.formValue (bound to the user-controlled text input via onChange in ClientSideXSSBase) is assigned directly to document.getElementById('targetDiv').innerHTML without sanitization. This bypasses React entirely and allows injection of arbitrary HTML and event handlers such as <div onmouseover=alert(1)>, enabling DOM-based XSS.

props.val is the raw response body fetched over unencrypted HTTP by App.fetchData (fetch('http://localhost:9000/inject')) and stored in state; it is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. An attacker who controls the remote endpoint or can perform a man-in-the-middle attack on the cleartext connection can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (XSS).

Content fetched over unencrypted HTTP in onClick (fetch('http://localhost:9000/inject'), line 15) is stored in state and rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. An attacker able to control the response (e.g. man-in-the-middle on the cleartext connection) can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that executes in the page (XSS from remote data).

The cors middleware is enabled with default options, which allows all origins (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). This permissive cross-domain policy lets any website retrieve this API's responses from a visitor's browser; combined with the /inject endpoints that serve active HTML/script content, it widens the attack surface for the client-side XSS sinks.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
